items.title: Cloud security basics for growing teams
items.excerpt: Five foundations that reduce the most risk for the least effort when your cloud footprint starts to grow.
items.body:
## Start with identity

Most cloud incidents begin with a compromised account. Enforce **multi-factor authentication** everywhere, remove shared accounts, and give people only the access their role needs.

## Know what you have

You cannot protect assets you cannot see. Keep an inventory of accounts, storage, databases and public endpoints, and review it regularly.

## Encrypt and back up

- Encrypt data at rest and in transit
- Keep backups separate from production credentials
- Test restores, not just backups

## Log everything that matters

Turn on audit logging for logins, configuration changes and data access, and send the logs somewhere an attacker cannot easily erase.

## Plan for the bad day

Write down who decides, who acts and who communicates when something goes wrong. A short, practised plan beats a long, unread one.

If you want help prioritising these for your own environment, [get in touch](/#contact).

items.title: How AI improves threat detection
items.excerpt: Why machine learning helps analysts find real attacks in a sea of events, and where human judgement still matters.
items.body:
## The volume problem

A modern cloud environment produces millions of events a day. No team can read them all, and rule-only detection either misses new behavior or drowns analysts in alerts.

## What AI adds

- **Baselines:** models learn what normal looks like for each user and workload
- **Anomaly spotting:** unusual locations, volumes or sequences stand out
- **Prioritisation:** related events are grouped and ranked by risk

## What it does not replace

AI is a force multiplier, not a substitute for analysts. People validate alerts, understand business context and decide how to respond.

## Practical tips

1. Feed models good, complete logs
2. Tune against your own environment
3. Review outcomes and feed lessons back in

Our [Threat Detection](/services/threat-detection) service combines both approaches.

items.title: Making compliance audit-ready all year
items.excerpt: Shift from a yearly scramble to continuous evidence so audits become routine.
items.body:
## Why audits feel painful

Evidence is gathered at the last minute from many people and systems. The fix is to collect it as part of normal work.

## Build it in

- Map each control to an **owner** and a **source of evidence**
- Automate evidence capture where you can, such as access reviews and configuration snapshots
- Keep policies short, current and easy to find

## Know your data

Auditors and customers will ask where sensitive data lives, who can access it and how it is protected. Maintain a simple data map and update it when systems change.

## Review on a schedule

Quarterly check-ins catch drift early and keep ownership clear.

See how [Compliance Management](/services/compliance-management) can support this.
